rv.q: “Rent” makes the musical theater joyously important again.
His gift for direct, compelling, colloquial lyrical statement seems to prove that the show tune can once again become both pertinent and popular.
We still are crazy about the piece, and are delighted that it will be around for a long time.
Rent , it seems, has grown with age, rather than tarnished.
'Rent' builds a genuine emotional momentum. His characters, based on Puccini's, become a self-created family we care about.
The move to Broadway has magnified the show's flaws.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this vibrant rock opera updating "La Bohème" for '90s East Village, praising its passionate score and raw energy, though some find its flaws magnified on Broadway.

vs.sum: An older theater in need of renovation, with virtually no rake in the orchestra — a tall person seated in front will block your view. First mezzanine row has a horizontal safety bar that partially obstructs sightlines. Legroom is tight throughout.

acc.note: Step-free main entrance to Orchestra. 6 wheelchair spaces. Personal induction loop devices available.
